chunks: Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

key_terms.مُحَدَّثَةٌ: Originated / Temporal / Created (as opposed to eternal)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for God's Will to be 'muḥadathah' (originated/temporal) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies divine 'Will' (al-Mashi'ah) as 'muḥadathah' (created/temporal), a pivotal stance in Shia kalam that aligns with the Akhbari and Usuli consensus against the Mu'tazilite view of Will as an eternal attribute distinct from Essence. This temporal nature underscores that God's Will is an act of His power manifesting in time, thereby preserving the absolute unity (Tawhid) of the Divine Essence while affirming His active engagement with creation.

en.ammaar-muslim: 4. [4/353] al-Kafi: A number of our companions from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhayna from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:
The Will (of God) is originated (temporal i.e. came into existence).
